newsitem.title: USA: Aetna to restructure, take Q3, Q4 charges.
newsitem.headline: Aetna to restructure, take Q3, Q4 charges.

text.p: Aetna Inc said on Thursday it would restructure its health care and retirement services units, resulting in the elimination of 4,000 jobs in healthcare and charges in the third and fourth quarters.
Aetna said it would take after-tax restructuring charges of about $32 million, or $0.22 per share, against third quarter earnings.
It said it would take an after-tax restructuring charge of about $275 million, or $1.82 per share, in the fourth quarter.
Aetna said the third quarter charge would cover severance and other costs in the Aetna Retirement Services unit, where a total of 400 jobs are to be cut by the end of the 1998 first quarter.

Fourth quarter charges will cover $68 million for asset writeoffs and $168 million in severance costs for Aetna U.S. Healthcare, where 4,000 job cuts are to be completed by the end of 1998, the company said.
First Call estimates for the company's third and fourth quarter earnings were not immediately available. Aetna said it expects to report third quarter results October 25.
Also included in fourth-quarter charges are $40 million for facilities-related writeoffs for Aetna U.S. Healthcare, created from Aetna's merger in July with U.S. Healthcare Inc.
Aetna said the restructuring moves are part of $300 million in after-tax savings it is seeking to achieve within 18 months of the merger.
For year-ago periods, Aetna reported operating earnings of $1.86 per share in the third quarter and $1.28 per share in the fourth quarter.
